title: Dopamine Farming™ Deck
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Tiny, playful actions for getting a little momentum. Choose only what feels comfortable.

cards.title: Make a tiny rhythm
cards.prompt: Whistle, snap, or clap a rhythm for 30 seconds.

cards.title: One-song task
cards.prompt: Try a “one-song task”: do one job for the length of one song.

cards.title: Tap, then begin
cards.prompt: Lightly tap your teeth together five times, then open your notes and begin.

cards.title: Balance and begin
cards.prompt: Balance a pencil on your fingertip for as long as you can, then start the task when it drops.

cards.title: A small checkpoint
cards.prompt: Keep a snack nearby and choose your own small checkpoint for enjoying one piece.

cards.title: A short sound detour
cards.prompt: Listen to a 15-second chunk of an unexpected music genre.

cards.title: Notice two textures
cards.prompt: Run your fingertips across two different textures, if that feels pleasant.

cards.title: Optional movement
cards.prompt: Try a few gentle hops or another movement that suits your body. You can also stay seated.

cards.title: Adjust the light
cards.prompt: If helpful, adjust the light to a level or tone that feels more comfortable.

title: NeuroScouts Quests Deck
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Creative imagination prompts. These are invitations, not assignments.

cards.title: Poem and drawing
cards.prompt: Write a short poem in the margins of a drawing. How do the words and images connect?

cards.title: Imagine a reviewer
cards.prompt: Read a stranger’s review online. Imagine their life story.

cards.title: A song someone likes
cards.prompt: Ask a friend for the last song they listened to. Write about how it makes you feel.

cards.title: Unusual job title
cards.prompt: Look up an unusual job title. Write about a person who has that job.

cards.title: Niche interest
cards.prompt: Explore a subreddit about a niche topic. Imagine someone deeply passionate about it.

cards.title: A found photograph
cards.prompt: Find a family photo of someone you don’t know. Imagine the relationships in it.

cards.title: Folklore remix
cards.prompt: Research the folklore of a culture you’re unfamiliar with. Write your own version of a tale.

cards.title: A book’s year
cards.prompt: Look up the year your favorite book was published. Write about how the world looked then.

cards.title: A curious law
cards.prompt: Search for an unusual law in another country. Imagine a day it is enforced.

cards.title: Voice-to-text stream
cards.prompt: Use voice-to-text to dictate a stream of consciousness, then reflect on the result. Skip this if voice input feels uncomfortable.

cards.title: A banned book
cards.prompt: Look up a banned book. Write why you think it was controversial.

cards.title: An ancient invention
cards.prompt: Explore an ancient invention. Write about how it shaped society.

cards.title: Where food comes from
cards.prompt: Find the origin of a favorite food. Write about the journey it took to your plate.

title: Real Life NeuroScouts
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Out-in-the-world prompts. Check accessibility and safety first; adapt or skip freely.

cards.title: Tell the quest story
cards.prompt: Write a short story about your quest. Use your experiences as inspiration.

cards.title: Staircase spotting
cards.prompt: Notice a staircase you can access. You can simply look, count the steps, or climb only if it feels safe and comfortable.

cards.title: Follow a path
cards.prompt: Choose a safe, accessible path to explore—or trace a route on a map from where you are.

title: Autistic Liberation Skill Cards
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Affirming prompts about comfort, autonomy, and self-expression. Some are bold; opt in only when they fit you and your situation.

cards.title: Wear what brings joy
cards.prompt: Wear something today that makes you happy instead of something that makes you blend in—even if it’s a playful backpack, a favorite shirt, or expressive socks.

cards.title: Move your own way
cards.prompt: If it feels safe, stim in a way that helps you. Your body does not exist only for other people’s comfort.

cards.title: Stay on your own side
cards.prompt: If someone looks at you funny, pause and remind yourself that being different does not make you a problem.

cards.title: Share your interest
cards.prompt: Talk about a favorite thing for as long as feels good today. You don’t need to apologize for enjoying it.

cards.title: Let laughter sound like you
cards.prompt: Laugh in the way that comes naturally, if you feel comfortable doing so.

cards.title: Bring a comfort object
cards.prompt: Carry a comfort object if it helps. It can be a practical support, not something to feel ashamed of.

cards.title: Choose a boundary
cards.prompt: Think of a boundary that protects your energy. You can keep it private or share it in your own words.

cards.title: Play for its own sake
cards.prompt: Choose a game that feels joyful and unserious—any age, any format.

cards.title: Enjoy an interest openly
cards.prompt: Choose an interest you love and give yourself permission to enjoy it.

cards.title: Release eye-contact pressure
cards.prompt: For one interaction, let yourself use the amount of eye contact that feels comfortable.

cards.title: Find autistic voices
cards.prompt: Find an autistic creator whose work feels good to you. Following them is optional.

cards.title: Use your own words
cards.prompt: If it feels right, describe yourself using the words that fit you. No label is required here.

cards.title: Let your voice be natural
cards.prompt: Let your voice be what it is today—quiet, excited, monotone, rambling, or something else.

cards.title: Use headphones
cards.prompt: Wear headphones in public if they help. You don’t owe strangers an explanation.

title: Playful Thinking Problem Solver
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Short thinking tools for when you want to examine a problem. Skip them when thinking itself feels like too much.

cards.title: Assumption check
cards.prompt: What are you assuming?

cards.title: Black hat
cards.prompt: What could go wrong? Consider this only if it helps you prepare, not spiral.

cards.title: Blue hat
cards.prompt: Summarize what you know and choose one next step—or decide to pause.

cards.title: Coin flip
cards.prompt: Heads: try it. Tails: change it. Treat the flip as a way to notice what you hope for, not as a rule.

cards.title: Combine
cards.prompt: Merge two parts of the problem or two possible solutions. What new option appears?

title: Care Quest Deck
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts (the PDF cover also credits SEHTLO WEBS MD)
description: A step-by-step guide for finding psychiatric care. This general resource may need adapting to your location and circumstances.

cards.title: Path 1 · Define the mission
cards.prompt: Choose a focus for care—or write “I don’t know, but I’m struggling.” Try to finish: “I’m seeking help because…”

cards.title: Path 2 · Choose the team
cards.prompt: Consider whether you’re looking for a therapist, psychiatrist, or both. If medication is a question for you, identify a qualified prescriber to discuss it with.

cards.title: Path 3 · Build a short list
cards.prompt: Write down a few possible providers from sources that apply where you live, such as your insurer, clinics, hospitals, or trusted recommendations.

cards.title: Path 4 · Check logistics
cards.prompt: Compare the practical details that matter to you: cost, location or telehealth, waiting time, coverage, and cancellation terms.

cards.title: Path 5 · Make contact
cards.prompt: If you feel ready, contact one option or ask someone to help. A backup option is okay too.

title: Frame Shifter Cards
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Choose one lens at a time to look at a problem differently. These are optional reflection prompts, not clinical techniques.

cards.title: Engineer mode
cards.prompt: Write the goal in one sentence. List a few real constraints and possible mechanisms, such as reduce, automate, buffer, or repeat. Choose one small test and decide how you’ll know it helped.

cards.title: Poet mode
cards.prompt: Write a few words connected to the problem. Combine two unrelated words into a sentence. What feeling or meaning does it bring up? Rewrite that insight plainly.

cards.title: Scientist mode
cards.prompt: Write a small hypothesis: “If X, then Y.” Choose a low-stakes test, try it only if you want to, and note what happened.

cards.title: Historian mode
cards.prompt: Has something like this happened before? What was the context then, and what has changed since?

cards.title: Philosopher mode
cards.prompt: Write the belief you’re holding. What supports it? What assumption sits underneath? Can you restate it more gently or precisely?

title: Design Thinking Solutions
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: A simple design process for a problem you have the energy to work on.

cards.title: Who is affected?
cards.prompt: Who is affected by this situation—including you?

cards.title: What is difficult?
cards.prompt: What part of this situation is difficult or frustrating for the people involved?

cards.title: Define
cards.prompt: In one sentence, what is the problem you want to address?

cards.title: Name the real problem
cards.prompt: Try completing: “The real problem is ____.” You can revise it later.

cards.title: Ideate
cards.prompt: Think of several possible ideas. Unusual ideas are allowed; you don’t need ten.

cards.title: List options
cards.prompt: List a few possible ideas, even if they’re rough.

cards.title: Prototype
cards.prompt: What is the smallest version of one idea you could try?

cards.title: What could you test today?
cards.prompt: What could you test today?

cards.title: Test
cards.prompt: Test.

title: Divergent Thinking Deck
author: Alora Young · NeuroScouts
description: Brief idea-generation prompts. No need to find a useful answer.

cards.title: Reimagine a spoon
cards.prompt: List five new uses for a spoon.

cards.title: Redesign a toothbrush
cards.prompt: How could you redesign a toothbrush to make it more fun?

cards.title: Give laces another job
cards.prompt: Invent three alternative purposes for shoelaces.
